subject: Follow-up: MeteorPay service disruption — customer-facing synopsis & action register
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@meteorpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick update: today’s service disruption at 10:00 UTC

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the patience this morning while we worked through the disruption that impacted your inference requests between ~10:00–10:35 UTC. I wanted to confirm we’re continuing to investigate root cause and will share a customer-facing summary with timeline and actions by EOD Friday (10/09).

Immediate notes: 
- Impact window: ~10:00–10:35 UTC; increased 5xxs and elevated tail latency for the embeddings route.
- Mitigated at 10:35 by failback to the high-availability model pool; traffic fully normalized by 10:40.

We’ll attach a short timeline and proposed remediation items for your review. If you’d like a working session with eng and CS tomorrow to walk through the timeline, say the word and I’ll schedule.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know this affected live traffic.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
--
Marcus Lin | marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick update: today’s service disruption at 10:00 UTC

Marcus / Marissa —

Preliminary engineering findings (short):
- Trigger: a regression in the runtime kernel selection logic pushed in the 09:50 UTC deploy; under specific sequence-length distribution we saw a cache-miss storm that amplified GPU memory pressure.
- Immediate cause: a fallback path to a non-quantized kernel activated incorrectly and prevented efficient KV-cache reuse.
- Why mitigation helped: routing to the HA pool forced a compatible model variant that avoided the regression.

I’ll finalize the RCA, timeline, and concrete code change and rollout checklist. Vivek will own the code patch; I’ll own the rollout plan and verification.

Hannah
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@meteorpay.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meteorpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Customer-facing synopsis: root cause, timeline, and actions (first draft)

Jordan / Alicia —

Per our commitment, attaching a short customer-facing summary of the event (attached PDF) and an action register we’ll track to completion. Highlights in plain language below — additional details are in the PDF and the action spreadsheet link.

Executive summary:
- What happened: Between 10:00–10:35 UTC on Oct 5, a serving runtime regression caused higher-than-normal error rates and elevated latency for a subset of inference requests.
- Impact: MeteorPay observed increased 5xx errors and delayed responses on API keys used for production traffic. The majority of affected calls were embeddings requests with mixed sequence lengths.
- Immediate mitigation: Traffic was redirected to a high-availability model pool at 10:35 UTC; error rates returned to baseline by 10:40 UTC.

Root cause (summary):
- A kernel-selection regression introduced in a deploy at 09:50 UTC incorrectly selected a fallback (non-quantized) execution path for certain inputs, causing inefficient KV cache reuse and memory pressure. This produced a cascade of cache misses and throttling inside the runtime.

Planned actions (owner / ETA):
1) Code patch and unit/regression tests (Vivek) — PR by 10/07, deploy to canary 10/08.
2) Expanded regression test (Hannah) — include sequence-length/quantization permutations by 10/12.
3) Customer verification session (Marcus / Marissa) — schedule for week of 10/12.
4) SLA credit assessment and technical verification for MeteorPay (Marissa) — proposal by 10/09.

Attachments: redwood_meteorpay_customer_synopsis_v1.pdf (concise RCA + timeline), action-register-meteorpay.xlsx (owners, due dates), timeline-20261005-1000-1200.csv (detailed event log).

If anything in this draft reads too technical for your stakeholders, we’ll redact specifics and keep a simple executive paragraph. Please let me know if you want us to remove any line items before we finalize.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--
Marcus Lin | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@meteorpay.com>

Subject: Re: Customer-facing synopsis: root cause, timeline, and actions (first draft)

Marcus,

Thank you — this is clear and helpful. A few requests from our side before you finalize: 
- Can you confirm the exact count of failed requests tied to our account during the window? We need the number for our internal incident report.
- We’d like a short one-paragraph executive summary (non-technical) suitable for our COO.
- Please include the proposed SLA credit calculation for the affected window (Marissa, looping you here).

Also — we’d like to schedule a 30-minute verification call with Hannah & Vivek during the week of 10/12 (UTC-friendly times). Alicia will send availability.

Thanks again for the timely follow-up.

— Jordan Park
Head of Platform Operations, MeteorPay
